discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Quantum optics and quantum information with superconducting circuits
motivation: The 2025 Prize recognised macroscopic quantum effects in electrical circuits. The nominees made the next conceptual step: circuit quantum electrodynamics. In 2004 Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed coupling a superconducting qubit to an on-chip microwave resonator, and showed experimentally that a single photon couples strongly to the artificial atom. This brought cavity QED into a regime of coupling strength and control that atoms in cavities cannot reach. Dispersive readout, photon-number-resolved spectroscopy, microwave Fock and cat states, bosonic codes and the quantum bus that links qubits all come from this architecture. Circuit QED is now the basis of nearly every superconducting quantum processor, including the demonstrations of below-threshold surface-code error correction. It also turned microwave quantum optics into a field of its own. A theory proposal led straight to a controllable quantum platform, and that platform became global infrastructure.
